record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.context_brief: Intermediate-pT hydro decoupling and quark scaling
record.original_question: How does hydrodynamic behavior decouple from hadron production at intermediate transverse momentum between a few and 10 GeV, where hadrons are increasingly poorly described by hydrodynamics but not yet fully described by perturbative-QCD jets, and what physical interpretation, if any, remains for constituent-quark scaling in that transition region?

evidence.quote: Amongst the many open questions and active areas of current research are: the elliptic flow of photons and heavy flavours, both measured to be typically larger than calculated by hydro; collectivity in small systems (discussed later); the hydro decoupling regime at intermediate pT of between a few and 10 GeV, where hadrons are increasingly less well described by hydro but not yet fully by pQCD and jets.
Quark scaling (NCQ) remains an intriguing regularity in the data, but unlike hydro has unfortunately not progressed much from the initial back-of-the envelope scaling relations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the bulk of low transverse momentum (pT ≲ 2 GeV) hadron production is well described by relativistic viscous hydrodynamics applied to a strongly coupled quark–gluon plasma, while the high-pT region (pT ≳ 10 GeV) is dominated by perturbative-QCD parton energy loss and jet fragmentation. In the intermediate window pT ∈ (a few GeV, 10 GeV), neither description is fully accurate. An empirical regularity known as constituent-quark-number (NCQ) scaling states that the elliptic flow v2 of identified hadrons satisfies, to good approximation,
   v2^h(pT) / n_h ≈ f(pT / n_h),
where n_h is the number of valence (constituent) quarks of hadron h (n_h = 2 for mesons, 3 for baryons), and f is a universal function.

Provide:

(a) A controlled, quantitative dynamical framework that interpolates between the hydrodynamic regime and the perturbative-QCD jet regime across the intermediate-pT window, and that specifies in what precise sense (e.g. for which observables, particle species, system sizes, and pT ranges) hydrodynamic behavior decouples from hadron production as pT increases through this window.

(b) A first-principles physical interpretation of constituent-quark-number scaling in this transition region: identify the underlying microscopic mechanism (for example quark recombination/coalescence at hadronization, or another mechanism) responsible for the approximate scaling relation above, derive the form of f and the expected magnitude and pattern of deviations from exact scaling as functions of pT, hadron species, collision energy, and system size, and explain whether NCQ scaling carries information about partonic degrees of freedom beyond what is captured by hydrodynamics or by pQCD.
artifact.status_search_result: The intermediate-pT regime between hydrodynamics and pQCD jets remains an active research area. Hybrid Hydro-Coal-Frag models (viscous hydro at low pT, quark coalescence at intermediate pT, and jet fragmentation at high pT) reproduce approximate NCQ scaling phenomenologically, supporting a coalescence/recombination interpretation, but a controlled first-principles description of the hydro-to-jet transition and a derivation of NCQ scaling beyond approximate scaling relations is not established. Recent (2024–2025) studies at RHIC continue to investigate the onset and breaking of NCQ scaling, indicating the underlying questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Onset of Constituent Quark Number Scaling in Heavy-Ion Collisions at RHIC
status_evidence.snippet: At lower collision energies NCQ scaling breaks down... as collision energy increases, a gradual onset of NCQ scaling is observed... signaling the emergence of partonic collectivity.
status_evidence.claim: NCQ scaling onset/breaking is still being studied as a signal of partonic degrees of freedom, indicating the interpretation question is active.

status_evidence.title: Number of constituent quark scaling of elliptic flows in high multiplicity p-Pb collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Hydro-Coal-Frag model combining viscous hydrodynamics at low pT, quark coalescence at intermediate pT, and jet fragmentation at high pT reproduces approximate NCQ scaling.
status_evidence.claim: Hybrid models phenomenologically describe the intermediate-pT region but do not yet provide a first-principles derivation.

status_evidence.title: Quark number scaling of pT spectra in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Experimental pT spectra exhibit constituent quark number scaling from RHIC to LHC, a direct consequence of the quark combination mechanism via equal velocity combination.
status_evidence.claim: Coalescence/combination is the leading proposed mechanism for NCQ scaling, but it remains a phenomenological scheme rather than a controlled derivation.
